policy: kill first; SPAN_UNDERIVED candidates are ineligible (R377 evidence-derivation requirement); R397 Phase 2: DOES_NOT_BEAT_BASELINE and PLAUSIBILITY_BOUND_VIOLATED candidates are ineligible for release (the machine's own physics gates the claim); among survivors prefer better E15-B verdict, then BEATS_BASELINE, then fewer deficient areas, then fewer UNCERTAIN attack outcomes; NO numeric score is computed (CEO standing rule: no new scoring systems)

ranked.mechanism: Temperature-dependent electrochemical impedance and contact resistance variability in battery systems
ranked.intervention: Implement a cold-weather diagnostic threshold in the BMS that increases the charging current minimum threshold or compensates voltage readings for low-temperature internal resistance changes at idle

ranked.mechanism: Thermal heterogeneity and in-plane temperature gradients within the battery alter electrochemical behavior, causing localized resistance changes that mimic or trigger intermittent sensor fault codes during low thermal mass conditions.
ranked.intervention: Implement a temperature-compensated voltage threshold algorithm for the battery monitoring unit that adjusts sensitivity based on real-time localized surface temperature readings rather than a static global threshold.

ranked.mechanism: Temperature-dependent internal resistance and electrochemical behavior in cells
ranked.intervention: Replace the voltage-sensing resistor or update the BMS temperature-compensation algorithm to account for increased internal resistance at sub-zero temperatures.

ranked.mechanism: Localized heat generation produces in-plane and through-thickness temperature gradients within lithium-ion cells, and these spatially non-uniform thermal distributions influence electrochemical behavior and safety, meaning that battery internal sensing must account for thermal heterogeneity rather than rely on a single-point measurement.
ranked.intervention: Map the paper's multiscale, gradient-aware thermal sensing concept onto the 2015 Camry's charging system by instrumenting the 12V lead-acid battery (and its sensing/ground paths) with distributed temperature sensors (surface-mounted plus embedded/ring-terminal sensors) combined with a model-predictive diagnostic that interprets spatially distributed thermal data instead of a single battery current/temperature sensor; at cold idle (<0 C) the alternator's reduced output combined with high accessory load on a cold-weakened battery creates localized internal heating/resistance gradients that the OEM IBS misreads as a charging fault.

ranked.mechanism: Thermal heterogeneity and spatial temperature gradients within the battery cell cause localized electrochemical non-uniformity, resulting in a temporary internal resistance spike or voltage dip that the vehicle's powertrain control module (PCM) misinterprets as a charging system fault when ambient temperature is low.
ranked.intervention: Implement embedded temperature sensors in the battery charging system to monitor in-plane and through-thickness temperature gradients, allowing the PCM to distinguish between actual charging faults and thermal-induced voltage transients.

ranked.mechanism: Cold-induced stiffening of battery electrolyte and solid-state interface changes increases internal impedance, which interacts with the vehicle's electrical load at idle to create voltage fluctuations that trigger the warning light; this effect is governed by the spatial distribution of heat generation which is insufficiently resolved at low temperatures.
ranked.intervention: Integrate a predictive modeling algorithm that uses indirect diagnostic methods (e.g., current load, ambient temperature) to estimate internal cell temperature and impedance, adjusting the threshold for the battery warning light accordingly.

selection_basis.intervention: Implement a cold-weather diagnostic threshold in the BMS that increases the charging current minimum threshold or compensates voltage readings for low-temperature internal resistance changes at idle
